subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Cooperative Games, Fair Play, and Lifetime Activity

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Name the movement cues for following rules and playing fairly and explain what each one does.
Show, describe, or diagram adapting a game so everyone can play. A demonstration, a spoken description, and a drawing are equally valid.
Apply cooperation and communication in a new movement task at a challenge level you select. Control and cue use are assessed, not speed, distance, or count.
A made-up learner is struggling with roles and turn-taking. Identify the likely cue or decision at fault, correct it, and explain why the correction helps.
Connect following rules and playing fairly with activities to enjoy outside class. Explain how one supports the other.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Adapt a familiar game so a learner with a different ability, size, or energy level can fully take part, then play it and review what worked.
Describe one way you adapted a task so it worked for you, and one activity from this unit you would choose to do again. There is no wrong answer here.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated cue use and control criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated movement concepts and decisions criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated application or performance criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated responsibility, safety, and inclusion criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. Using the adapted alternative is a full-credit path, never a reduced one.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Cooperative Games, Fair Play, and Lifetime Activity?
